references.text: Matthew's parallel list of the apostles mentions the same names: Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, and Simon the Cananaean (the Zealot), corresponding to those mentioned in Luke 6:15.
Mark's list of the apostles includes among others James son of Alphaeus and Simon the Cananaean, who are the same apostles mentioned in Luke 6:15.
Acts repeats the list of the apostles after Jesus' ascension, mentioning among others Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, and Simon the Zealot—the same as in Luke 6:15.
Thomas, who is mentioned in Luke 6:15, is referred to here by the nickname Didymus (the Twin), providing closer identification of this apostle.
Thomas, one of the apostles mentioned in Luke 6:15, asks Jesus a question during the Last Supper, revealing his character and role among the disciples.
Matthew (Levi) is called by Jesus to follow him. This is the same Matthew mentioned in the list of apostles in Luke 6:15.
Thomas, mentioned in Luke 6:15, is known for his doubt after Jesus' resurrection, providing further background on this apostle.
